headline: Margins improve, one-time gain flatters net income
summary_short: Revenue rose to $5.71B (+3.7% y/y, +5.8% q/q) as international growth offset Middle East softness; operating income grew 7.0% y/y to $778M and net income rose 13.1% y/y to $534M, partly aided by a $95M one-time net credit.
summary_long: Both segments grew sequentially: Completion & Production +6% on Western Hemisphere stimulation and Asia well intervention, offset by the chemical-business sale and softer Middle East activity; Drilling & Evaluation +5% on North America/Europe drilling and wireline, though its operating income fell 4% q/q on a software-sales roll-off. North America revenue rose 7% q/q; Middle East/Asia fell 2% q/q on regional geopolitical conflict. GAAP EPS of $0.64 beat adjusted EPS of $0.55 by $0.09, entirely from a $95M net pre-tax credit (equity-investment gains, partly offset by a divestiture loss). Cash ended at $2.05B, long-term debt flat at $7.07B; the company returned ~$200M via buybacks plus $0.17/share dividends. No forward guidance was given.
